{{nihongo|'''Shizuhi Shrine'''|静火神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kii Province]].

[[File:Shizuhi-jinja kyuuchi.JPG|thumb|250px|right|Former site monument of Shizuhi Shrine (foreground) and Mount Yakushi, where the current shrine stands]]
'''Shizuhi Shrine''' (しずひじんじゃ / しづひじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Wada, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|Q131314|qid=Q131314}}{{ill|Wakayama (city)|Q200747|qid=Q200747}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}. Today, it is an extramural subsidiary shrine of {{ill|Kamayama Shrine|Q11597743|qid=Q11597743}}.

Together with {{ill|Itate Shrine|Q11380847|qid=Q11380847|lt=Date Shrine}} (Sonobe, Wakayama City) and {{ill|Shima Shrine|Q17212913|qid=Q17212913}} ({{ill|Nakanoshima|Q17226981|qid=Q17226981|lt=Nakanoshima}}, Wakayama City), it is known as the “Ki Sansho-sha” (Three Shrines of Ki) {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine Site (Heibonsha)|1983|p=376}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
The enshrined deity is the following single kami {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987|p=99}}:
:* Shizuhi Ōkami

According to documents of the Ugai clan, the shrine’s hereditary priests, the deity was identified as {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|Q1640658|qid=Q1640658|lt=Hi-no-Musubi no Kami}} {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987|p=99}}. Another theory, found in the *Zoku Fudoki*, holds that the “Ki Sansho-sha” were branch enshrinements of the three deities of Isonokami—Itsu no Take no Mikoto, Ōyatsuhime no Mikoto, and Tsumatsuhime no Mikoto—and identifies the deity of Shizuhi Shrine as Tsumatsuhime no Mikoto {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine Site (Heibonsha)|1983|p=376}}. Yet another view considers Shizuhi to have been a “fire-quelling deity” of Kii Province, known as the “Land of Trees” {{Sfn|Kamayama Shrine and Shizuhi Shrine (Kami-gami)|1986|pp=316–318}}. In addition, the *{{ill|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|Q11381815|qid=Q11381815}}* states that Funatama Shrine, a subsidiary shrine of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}}, was the clan deity of the Ki clan and the main shrine of “Shima Shrine, Shizuhi Shrine, and Date Shrine.”

=== History ===
=== Founding ===
The date of founding is unknown. Originally, the shrine stood about 200 meters east of its current location ({{Coord|34|12|9.46|N|135|12|37.07|E|region:JP-30_type:landmark|name=Former site of Shizuhi Shrine}}) {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987|p=99}}. According to the *Zoku Fudoki*, Shizuhi Shrine had fallen into ruin before the {{ill|Einin|Q1327307|qid=Q1327307}} era ({{ill|1293|Q5557|qid=Q5557}}–{{ill|1299|Q5564|qid=Q5564}}), but a document of the Hinokuma Shrine from {{ill|Chōkyō|Q968843|qid=Q968843}} 1 ({{ill|1487|Q6652|qid=Q6652}}) records that one *to* of ritual rice was allocated to Shizuhi Shrine {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine Site (Heibonsha)|1983|p=376}}. According to the *Nanki Tokugawa-shi*, by around {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 8 ({{ill|1723|Q6921|qid=Q6921}}) the shrine had again fallen into ruin; in that same year, Wakayama Domain rebuilt the shrine buildings on Mount Yakushi (Maeyama / Amagiri-yama; the present site), and Kamayama Shrine assumed its administration {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine Site (Heibonsha)|1983|p=376}}.

=== Overview ===
In the national histories, together with Date Shrine and Shima Shrine (Shima Jinja), Shizuhi Shrine is recorded as having received promotions in divine rank: from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade in {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 11 ({{ill|844|Q23835|qid=Q23835}}); to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade in {{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}} 3 ({{ill|850|Q30364|qid=Q30364}}); to Senior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade in {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 1 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}); and to Junior Third Rank in Jōgan 17 ({{ill|875|Q23816|qid=Q23816}}) {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine Site (Heibonsha)|1983|p=376}}.

In the *{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}* *{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}*, it is listed under {{ill|Kii Province|Q864053|qid=Q864053}}{{ill|Nagusa district|Q11415547|qid=Q11415547}} as “Shizuhi Shrine, Myōjin Grand Shrine,” placing it among the {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}; the *{{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|Q17210008|qid=Q17210008}}* records it as “Senior First Rank, Shizuhi Ōkami” {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine Site (Heibonsha)|1983|p=376}}. In all cases, it is ranked higher than Kamayama Shrine.

It is said that together with {{ill|Itate Shrine|Q11380847|qid=Q11380847|lt=Date Shrine}} (Sonobe, Wakayama City) and {{ill|Shima Shrine|Q17212913|qid=Q17212913}} ({{ill|Nakanoshima|Q17226981|qid=Q17226981|lt=Nakanoshima}}, Wakayama City), it was known as the “Ki Sansho-sha” {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=362}}. References to the Ki Sansho-sha appear beginning with a rice storage ledger from {{ill|Eishō (Heian period)|Q1193549|qid=Q1193549}} 3 ({{ill|1048|Q19359|qid=Q19359}}), as well as in the *{{ill|Chūyūki|Q11363231|qid=Q11363231}}* entry for {{ill|Tennin (era)|Q1193599|qid=Q1193599}} 2 ({{ill|1109|Q19515|qid=Q19515}}) and in the four-verse sacred songs of the *{{ill|Ryōjin Hishō|Q3010584|qid=Q3010584}}* {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=362}}. According to the *{{ill|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|Q11381815|qid=Q11381815}}*, the origin of the Ki Sansho-sha lies in the three ships used by {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} for the {{ill|Three Han Campaign|Q11249435|qid=Q11249435}}, which she had {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}} enshrine {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=362}}.

Furthermore, since Wada Village was formerly a shrine estate of {{ill|Hinokuma Shrine|Q888184|qid=Q888184}}, the deity of Shizuhi was closely connected with those shrines and with the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q11604953|qid=Q11604953|lt=hereditary governors of Kii Province}}. At Kusa-no-miya, enshrined within the grounds of those shrines, it is said that on September 15 the deity of Shizuhi made a sacred procession and the Shizuhi Festival was held {{Sfn|Kamayama Shrine and Shizuhi Shrine (Kami-gami)|1986|pp=316–318}}.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}; however, in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 42 ({{ill|1909|Q2057|qid=Q2057}}) it was merged into Inari Shrine, a subsidiary shrine of Kamayama Shrine {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine Site (Heibonsha)|1983|p=376}}{{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987|p=99}}. In {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 25 ({{ill|1950|Q18597|qid=Q18597}}), shrine buildings were constructed on the original Mount Yakushi site and the deity was transferred there {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987|p=99}}.

** {{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}} 3 ({{ill|850|Q30364|qid=Q30364}}) 10th month, 21st day: Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (*{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Montoku Tennó Džicuroku|de|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|ff|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon Montoku tennō jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|ko|일본문덕천황실록|pt|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|zh|日本文德天皇實錄|qid=Q1052905}}*) – recorded as “Shizuhi no Kami.”
